packet.headline_seed: Anthropic launches Claude Sonnet 5 as a cheaper way to run agents
packet.description_seed: Anthropic’s Claude Sonnet 5 brings stronger agentic capabilities, lower pricing, and improved safety, positioning the model as a cheaper alternative to Opus, GPT-5.5, and Gemini Pro.

what: Anthropic launches Claude Sonnet 5 as a cheaper way to run agents

clean_source_blocks.text: The release, which Anthropic describes as "the most agentic Sonnet model yet," makes Sonnet 5 the default model for users on Anthropic's Free and Pro plans, while also making it available to Max, Team, and Enterprise customers. Introductory API pricing is set at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens through August 31, after which it rises to $3 and $15 respectively — still well below the $5 input and $25 output pricing of Anthropic's top-of-the-line Opus 4.8. The strategic logic is unmistakable: Anthropic is trying to democratize access to capabilities that until very recently only its most expensive models could deliver, while building the kind of broad-based developer adoption that will look attractive in an S-1 filing.

Credit: VentureBeat made with Midjourney Anthropic today released Claude Sonnet 5, a new AI model that the company says delivers near-flagship performance at mid-tier prices — a move designed to give cost-conscious enterprise developers access to powerful agentic capabilities just as the San Francisco-based AI lab barrels toward an initial public offering that will test whether the private market's staggering AI valuations can survive public scrutiny.

Sonnet 5 narrowed the gap with Anthropic's flagship Opus model across five major evaluations, and surpassed it on one. (Source: Anthropic) Sonnet 5 posts major gains over its predecessor, Sonnet 4.6, across every evaluation Anthropic disclosed. On SWE-bench Pro, an agentic coding benchmark, Sonnet 5 scores 63.2% compared with Sonnet 4.6's 58.1% — a jump that brings it within striking distance of Opus 4.8's 69.2%. On Terminal-Bench 2.1, another coding evaluation, the gap narrows further: 80.4% for Sonnet 5 versus 67.0% for Sonnet 4.6 and 82.7% for Opus 4.8.

In multidisciplinary reasoning, as measured by Humanity's Last Exam, Sonnet 5 scores 43.2% without tools and 57.4% with tools — the latter figure essentially matching Opus 4.8's 57.9%. On computer use tasks evaluated through OSWorld-Verified, Sonnet 5 reaches 81.2%, up from 78.5%. And on GDPval-AA v2, a knowledge-work benchmark, it scores 1,618 — surpassing Opus 4.8's 1,615 and far exceeding Sonnet 4.6's 1,395. The pattern across these evaluations tells a consistent story: Sonnet 5 doesn't merely inch forward from its predecessor. It vaults into a performance tier that overlaps substantially with Anthropic's flagship model, while costing roughly 60% less per token at standard pricing and even less during the

payload.title: Anthropic julkaisi Claude Sonnet 5:n edullisemmaksi malliksi tekoälyagenteille
payload.summary: Anthropicin uusi Claude Sonnet 5 tuo yhtiön mukaan lähes lippulaivamallin suorituskykyä selvästi alempaan hintaluokkaan. Malli tulee oletukseksi Free- ja Pro-käyttäjille ja saataville myös yritysasiakkaille.
payload.content:
Anthropic on julkaissut Claude Sonnet 5 -tekoälymallin, jota yhtiö kuvaa tähän asti agenttimaisimmaksi Sonnet-mallikseen. Julkaisu tähtää erityisesti kehittäjiin ja yrityksiin, jotka tarvitsevat vahvoja automaatio- ja koodaustoimintoja mutta eivät halua maksaa Opus-lippulaivamallin hintatasoa.

## Uusi oletusmalli useille käyttäjille

Claude Sonnet 5:stä tulee oletusmalli Anthropicin Free- ja Pro-tilaajille. Lisäksi se on saatavilla Max-, Team- ja Enterprise-asiakkaille, mikä laajentaa mallin käyttöä sekä yksittäisille käyttäjille että organisaatioille.

API-hinnoittelu alkaa kampanjahinnalla: miljoona syötetokenia maksaa 2 dollaria ja miljoona tuotostokenia 10 dollaria elokuun loppuun asti. Sen jälkeen hinnat nousevat 3 ja 15 dollariin. Vertailun vuoksi Anthropic hinnoittelee Opus 4.8:n 5 dollariin miljoonalta syötetokenilta ja 25 dollariin miljoonalta tuotostokenilta.

Hinnoittelu kertoo yhtiön pyrkimyksestä tuoda aiemmin kalleimpiin malleihin liitettyjä ominaisuuksia laajempaan käyttöön. Samalla Anthropic hakee asemaa kehittäjien työkaluna tilanteessa, jossa tekoälymallien kustannukset vaikuttavat suoraan siihen, kuinka laajasti agentteja voidaan ajaa tuotantokäytössä.

## Tulokset lähestyvät Opus-mallia

Anthropic kertoo Sonnet 5:n parantaneen tuloksiaan Sonnet 4.6:een verrattuna kaikissa julkistetuissa arvioinneissa. SWE-bench Pro -koodausvertailussa Sonnet 5 sai tuloksen 63,2 prosenttia, kun Sonnet 4.6:n tulos oli 58,1 prosenttia ja Opus 4.8:n 69,2 prosenttia.

Terminal-Bench 2.1 -testissä Sonnet 5 ylsi 80,4 prosenttiin. Sonnet 4.6:n tulos oli 67,0 prosenttia ja Opus 4.8:n 82,7 prosenttia. Monialaisessa päättelyssä Humanity's Last Exam -testissä Sonnet 5 sai ilman työkaluja 43,2 prosenttia ja työkalujen kanssa 57,4 prosenttia, mikä oli lähellä Opus 4.8:n 57,9 prosentin tulosta.

OSWorld-Verified-tehtävissä Sonnet 5 nousi 81,2 prosenttiin aiemmasta 78,5 prosentista. GDPval-AA v2 -tietotyövertailussa se sai 1 618 pistettä, hieman Opus 4.8:n 1 615 pisteen edelle ja selvästi yli Sonnet 4.6:n 1 395 pisteen. Julkistettujen lukujen perusteella Sonnet 5 sijoittuu monessa tehtävässä lähelle Anthropicin kalleinta mallia, mutta standardihinnoilla noin 60 prosenttia alemmalla tokenikohtaisella kustannuksella.

Anthropic kertoo mallin lähestyvän Opus 4.8:n suorituskykyä useissa koodaus-, päättely- ja tietotyötesteissä.

article.title: Anthropic julkaisi Claude Sonnet 5:n edullisemmaksi malliksi tekoälyagenteille
article.description: Anthropicin uusi Claude Sonnet 5 tuo yhtiön mukaan lähes lippulaivamallin suorituskykyä selvästi alempaan hintaluokkaan. Malli tulee oletukseksi Free- ja Pro-käyttäjille ja saataville myös yritysasiakkaille.
article.research:
[Lähde: VentureBeat]
Credit: VentureBeat made with Midjourney

Anthropic today released Claude Sonnet 5, a new AI model that the company says delivers near-flagship performance at mid-tier prices — a move designed to give cost-conscious enterprise developers access to powerful agentic capabilities just as the San Francisco-based AI lab barrels toward an initial public offering that will test whether the private market's staggering AI valuations can survive public scrutiny.

The release, which Anthropic describes as "the most agentic Sonnet model yet," makes Sonnet 5 the default model for users on Anthropic's Free and Pro plans, while also making it available to Max, Team, and Enterprise customers. Introductory API pricing is set at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens through August 31, after which it rises to $3 and $15 respectively — still well below the $5 input and $25 output pricing of Anthropic's top-of-the-line Opus 4.8.

The strategic logic is unmistakable: Anthropic is trying to democratize access to capabilities that until very recently only its most expensive models could deliver, while building the kind of broad-based developer adoption that will look attractive in an S-1 filing.

Sonnet 5 narrowed the gap with Anthropic's flagship Opus model across five major evaluations, and surpassed it on one. (Source: Anthropic)

Sonnet 5 posts major gains over its predecessor, Sonnet 4.6, across every evaluation Anthropic disclosed. On SWE-bench Pro, an agentic coding benchmark, Sonnet 5 scores 63.2% compared with Sonnet 4.6's 58.1% — a jump that brings it within striking distance of Opus 4.8's 69.2%. On Terminal-Bench 2.1, another coding evaluation, the gap narrows further: 80.4% for Sonnet 5 versus 67.0% for Sonnet 4.6 and 82.7% for Opus 4.8.

In multidisciplinary reasoning, as measured by Humanity's Last Exam, Sonnet 5 scores 43.2% without tools and 57.4% with tools — the latter figure essentially matching Opus 4.8's 57.9%. On computer use tasks evaluated through OSWorld-Verified, Sonnet 5 reaches 81.2%, up from 78.5%. And on GDPval-AA v2, a knowledge-work benchmark, it scores 1,618 — surpassing Opus 4.8's 1,615 and far exceeding Sonnet 4.6's 1,395.

The pattern across these evaluations tells a consistent story: Sonnet 5 doesn't merely inch forward from its predecessor. It vaults into a performance tier that overlaps substantially with Anthropic's flagship model, while costing roughly 60% less per token at standard pricing and even less during the
